dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of the Human Immunodeficiency Virus and Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017
Passed by the Parliament of India, The Human Immunodeficiency Virus and Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017 came into force to safeguard the legal and human rights of persons infected and affected by HIV and AIDS. The legislation provides a statutory framework to prevent social stigma, discrimination, and breaches of confidentiality. 
1. Objectives of the Act
The primary objectives of the legislation include:
•	Prevention and Control: To curb and manage the spread of HIV and AIDS across the country. 
•	Combating Stigma: To address and eliminate widespread social stigma and discrimination directed against Persons Living with HIV (PLHIV) and those closely affected by them. 
•	Protecting Rights: To legally secure and reinforce fundamental human rights, such as the right to healthcare, employment, education, and property. 
•	Ensuring Accountability: To establish structured mechanisms for grievance redressal and penalize acts of discrimination or privacy breaches. 
2. Key Provisions
A. Prohibition of Discrimination
The Act strictly prohibits unfair treatment or discrimination against "protected persons" (defined as any HIV-positive person or anyone who resides/has resided with an HIV-positive person) across multiple domains: 
•	Employment: Forbids denial or termination of employment, or unfair bias in occupation. 
•	Healthcare & Education: Prohibits denying entry, treatment, or educational services, or segregating students/patients. 
•	Housing and Property: Protects the right to rent, purchase, or reside in property without obstruction. 
•	Public/Private Office: Ensures they can stand for public or private offices. 
•	Insurance: Prevents unfair denial or differential pricing of life/health insurance policies without actuarial justification.
B. Informed Consent and Testing
•	No Forced Testing: Compulsory HIV testing cannot be mandated as a pre-requisite for employment, securing healthcare, or accessing other services, except in specific scenarios mandated by court orders. 
•	Informed Consent: Prior, voluntary, and informed consent is mandatory before conducting an HIV test, initiating medical treatment, or entering a person into medical research. 
C. Right to Confidentiality
•	Privacy Maintenance: The HIV status of an individual is strictly confidential. 
•	Exceptions: Disclosure is permissible only with the explicit written consent of the individual, or when mandated by a competent court order in the interest of justice. Healthcare providers are bound to maintain privacy regarding a patient's status. 
D. Healthcare and Treatment Rights
•	Access to Treatment: The Central and State Governments are mandated to take measures to provide, as far as possible, diagnostic facilities, Anti-Retroviral Therapy (ART), and Opportunistic Infection Management to PLHIV. 
•	Guardianship of Minors: Special provisions protect the property and welfare rights of children affected by HIV/AIDS, allowing them or their representatives to approach Child Welfare Committees for safeguard support. 
E. Prevention of Hate Speech
•	The Act prohibits any individual from publishing, broadcasting, or propagating feelings of hatred, discrimination, or physical violence against protected persons through spoken words, written material, signs, or visible representations. 
F. Grievance Redressal and Compliance Mechanisms
•	Complaints Officer: Every establishment (corporate body, cooperative society, or institution meeting statutory criteria) must designate a Complaints Officer to handle internal grievances regarding violations of the Act. 
•	Ombudsman: State Governments are required to appoint an Ombudsman to hear and decide legal appeals and complaints against establishments that fail to comply with the legislation.
3. Penalties for Non-Compliance
To enforce strict compliance, the Act prescribes penalties for violations:
•	Breach of Confidentiality or Discrimination: Disclosing an individual's HIV status without authorization or violating provisions of the Act can attract imprisonment ranging from 3 months up to 2 years, and/or a fine of up to 1 Lakh Rupees. 
•	Spreading Hatred: Engaging in acts promoting hatred or physical violence against protected persons is similarly punishable under the legal penalties framework.

dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of the Bombay Revenue Jurisdiction Act 1876
.
Summary Points

1.	Short Title & Commencement:
•	Short Title: "The Bombay Revenue Jurisdiction Act, 1876"
•	Commencement: Immediate for most parts, with a specific section to commence on a date directed by the Governor General in Council.
2.	Extent: - Applies to all of the State of Maharashtra (then referred to by other names in amendments).
•	Exceptions include suits regarding revenue assessment in the City of Bombay and certain specified Acts.
3.	Definitions: - Land and Land-Revenue broadly defined to include various rights, payments, and sums related to land.
4.	Bar of Certain Suits (Section 4):
•	Prohibited Matters in Civil Courts:
•	Claims against the Government related to hereditary officer properties, certain land grants, and more.
•	Objections to land-revenue assessments, mode, or notifications.
•	Claims arising from land-revenue realization proceedings.
•	Specific entry, omission, or amendment claims in revenue records.
•	Distribution of land on estate partition under certain Acts.
•	Claims for land free from land-revenue payment, certain payments, and waste land occupation.
•	Boundary disputes under specific Acts.
•	Exceptions (Proviso): Allows civil court jurisdiction for claims based on explicit exemptions by enactment, specific grants, or judicial/adjudicative decisions.
5.	Other Provisions: - Bar of Suits against Revenue Officers (Section 6) for bona fide acts.
•	Punishment/Prosecution of Revenue Officers does not bar civil remedies (Section 7).
•	Requirement to Exhaust Appeal Rights before suing (Section 11).
•	Power of State Government to Refer Questions to the High Court (Section 12).

(a) that such drain be closed, discontinued or destroyed and that any work necessary for that purpose be done; or

dc.identifier.next_section.value: 25.Power to close railway opened for the public carriage of passengers.

dc.identifier.section_page_note.value:
When an accident has occurred on a railway resulting in a temporary suspension of traffic, and either the original lines of rails and works have been restored to their original standard or a temporary diversion has been laid for the purpose of restoring communication, the original lines of rails and works so restored, or the temporary diversion, as the case may be, may, without prior inspection by the Commissioner, be opened for the public carriage of passengers, subject to the following conditions, namely:--
(a) the railway servant incharge of the works undertaken by reason of the accident has certified in writing that the opening of the restored lines of rails and works, or of the temporary diversion will not in his opinion be attended with danger to the public; and
